objective: Running a Daily Scrum as the Developers' planning event rather than a status report
secondaryObjectives: Applying the three pillars -- transparency, inspection and adaptation -- to spot where a team has stopped inspecting or adapting
Recognizing the five Scrum values in a team's behavior and what happens when they erode
Causing the removal of impediments to the team's progress without solving everything for them
Recognizing Scrum anti-patterns -- the Scrum Master as task assigner, a status-report Daily Scrum, a stabilization Sprint -- and responding to them
Deciding what happens to work that does not meet the Definition of Done when the Sprint ends
Leading the organization's Scrum adoption: training, coaching and helping stakeholders work with the team

brief.situation: You are the Scrum Master of the checkout team at Harbor Lane Outfitters, a fictional online outdoor-gear shop. Sprint 14 runs one week, Monday 1 March to Friday 5 March 2027. Sprint Planning ended at 13:00 on Monday with a Sprint Goal: a returning shopper can pay with a saved card at checkout. Rob, the engineering manager, has started coming to the Daily Scrum because, he says, he never knows where things stand.
handover: Developers: Lena, Sam, Priya and Dev. Product Owner: Maya.

Sprint Backlog: 29 points. Save a card on file, pay with a saved card, and the checkout tests and accessibility pass deliver the Sprint Goal; the card-expiry email and the flaky test fix are in the Sprint too.
howItWorks: The dashboard shows the commitments, the board, the burn-down, impediments, the people and the events. You act as the Scrum Master from the action groups; each action takes the time it would.
Move the week on to the next Daily Scrum when you are ready. Each morning the board shows what the Developers got done the day before.
On Friday you hold the Sprint Review and the Retrospective, then write a short reflection.

dailyScrum.title: Tuesday, 09:15: the Daily Scrum
dailyScrum.context: The Developers gather at the board. Rob arrives with a notebook and says: "Let's go round. Each of you, what did you do yesterday and what's the status?" Lena looks at you.

choices.label: Let Rob run it: each Developer reports their status to him

effects.log: 35 minutes of status reports to Rob. Nobody mentions the Sprint Goal.

choices.feedback: The Daily Scrum is the Developers' event to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt their plan, in 15 minutes. A report to a manager hides what is in the way.

choices.label: Ask the Developers to plan their day toward the Sprint Goal at the board; ask Rob to listen, and offer him time afterwards

effects.finding: Lena: "Save a card is stuck. No sandbox keys from security." Priya: "Then I'll leave the expiry emails and pair with Sam on paying with a saved card."

effects.log: 12 minutes. The Developers re-plan their day toward the Sprint Goal; an impediment is out in the open.

choices.feedback: That is the Daily Scrum's purpose. Rob still needs a way to see progress: the board, the burn-down and the Sprint Review.

choices.label: Run it yourself: each person answers the three questions to you

effects.finding: Asked about impediments, Lena mentions the missing sandbox keys. Nobody re-plans; Priya goes back to the expiry emails.

effects.log: 25 minutes, everyone reporting to the Scrum Master.

choices.feedback: The impediment surfaced, but the Developers reported to you instead of planning together. The 2020 Guide dropped the three questions: the Developers choose any structure that serves the Sprint Goal.

choices.label: Cancel today's Daily Scrum; everyone is busy

effects.log: No Daily Scrum: nothing inspected, nothing adapted.

choices.feedback: Skipping it removes the daily inspection and adaptation the Sprint depends on.

reflection.question: Reflect on the Sprint: what was going wrong with the Daily Scrum and the board, what you did about the impediment and the team's focus, and what the Sprint Review showed and why.

parts.label: The Daily Scrum and transparency
parts.criteria: Names the status-report Daily Scrum as an anti-pattern: the event is the Developers' 15-minute planning toward the Sprint Goal, and status reports hid the stuck item and the drift in focus; Rob's need was met another way (the board, the burn-down, the Sprint Review).
parts.modelAnswer: The Daily Scrum had become a status report to Rob. Its purpose is for the Developers to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt their plan, in 15 minutes. Run that way, the stuck item and Priya's work off the Goal came out at once. Rob got his transparency through the board, the burn-down and an invitation to the Sprint Review.

parts.label: Impediment, self-management and Done
parts.criteria: Caused the impediment's removal outside the team the same day rather than working around the Definition of Done; left the plan to the Developers instead of assigning tasks; showed only Done work at the Review and returned anything undone to the Product Backlog; chose a Retrospective improvement.
parts.modelAnswer: The missing sandbox keys were outside the team, so I took them to the security lead and stayed on it; a mock would have broken the Definition of Done. I asked the Developers how their plan served the Goal and left the plan to them. At the Review we showed only the Done Increment; anything not Done goes back to the Product Backlog. The Retrospective picked one improvement for next Sprint.

expertPath.text: Let the Developers start; the Sprint Goal and the board are set.
Hand the Daily Scrum back to the Developers: plan the day toward the Sprint Goal in 15 minutes, with Rob listening. The stuck item and the drifting focus come out.
Take the missing sandbox keys to the security lead and stay on it; meet Rob and show him the board, the burn-down and the Review.
Show only the Done Increment, say what is not Done, and choose one improvement at the Retrospective.

goalMet.headline: Good: the Sprint Goal, the Scrum way
goalMet.body: The Daily Scrum became the Developers' planning event again, the impediment was raised the same day, Rob got transparency through the artifacts, and the Review showed only Done work.

gaps.headline: Goal met, with gaps
gaps.body: The Increment is Done, but the criteria below show what was late or missing: the Daily Scrum, the impediment, Rob, or the Retrospective.

goalMissed.headline: Goal missed, honestly
goalMissed.body: The Review was transparent, which keeps empiricism working. The criteria show what cost the Goal: the impediment raised late, the Daily Scrum that hid it, or focus off the Goal.

undone.headline: Undone work shown as finished
undone.body: An item that does not meet the Definition of Done 'cannot be released or even presented at the Sprint Review' (Scrum Guide 2020). It goes back to the Product Backlog.

broken.headline: A working relationship broke
broken.body: Assigning tasks takes the Sprint Backlog from the Developers; status reports and no other window into progress leave a manager uneasy. Both erode respect and openness.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: The Sprint was not closed before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: The Daily Scrum is the Developers' 15-minute event to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the plan; a status report to a manager hides problems. Hand it back, give the manager transparency through the board, the burn-down and the Sprint Review, cause the removal of the outside impediment the same day instead of mocking around the Definition of Done, leave the plan to the Developers, show only the Done Increment, and leave the Retrospective with one improvement.
